items.full_text_snippet: Goldman Sachs has restricted Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub to its engineers, cutting off traders and bankers who used the tools to track client flows and build market models. The bank barred its Hong Kong bankers from Claude in April and is now a lead underwriter on Anthropic's IPO. Most traders and bankers at Goldman Sachs can no longer use AI coding tools at work. Internal guidance updated in October restricts Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub to the bank's engineers, Bloomberg News reported , following a review of productivity and risk concerns. Strats, who work across trading, quantitative research and software engineering, still have access, according to a second person familiar with the matter. The change has frustrated some traders, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. They had been using the tools to monitor client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and put together written and graphic material. Goldman spokesperson Nick Carcaterra said the bank makes certain AI tools available to staff "to determine the best use cases" across the firm. Argenti was praising trader-built tools in July As recently as July, chief information officer Marco Argenti was talking up "vibe coding" by Goldman's non-technical employees. He told Bloomberg that traders and bankers had built tools with AI and passed them to the firm's engineers, of whom there are about 12,000, to be improved. That arrangement let the people closest to a problem build a first version without waiting for engineering time. It also meant thousands of employees without engineering training were running software that writes and executes code, on the same machines they use to handle client information. At a conference in Turin last month, Argenti described Goldman's AI adoption in waves and said developers, more than 12,000 of the bank's roughly 47,000 staff, had made up the first. items.summary: A memo circulated earlier this year reportedly claimed that China’s Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive to spy on Nvidia's CEO.
items.full_text_snippet: A memo circulated earlier this year claimed that technology executive Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to multiple media reports. The New York Times, which had previously said Nvidia’s chief executive had been the target of Chinese intelligence, was the first to report on the memo . The Financial Times subsequently reported that the memo — supposedly based on U.S. intelligence — also claimed Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed. An Nvidia spokesperson told the NYT that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual,” and that the company does not share classified information with its customers. A separate NYT report examined New Matrix, a Chinese company authorized by the U.S. Commerce Department to buy advanced Nvidia chips. At the office address listed by New Matrix, reporters only found “a hollow gray shell,” raising concerns that it could be a front for a blacklisted private equity firm. The Nvidia spokesperson said the company sells “the first, best and most of our technology in America.”

items.summary: HN 热门讨论（72 points, 50 评论）by kyunez
items.full_text_snippet: If you work with Claude Code or Codex from the terminal, you know this one. You start a task. The AI takes time to reply, so you start another one. Then the first one replies, but the reply needs one clarification, one follow up and one side task — and each of them wants its own tab. Then the second tab's reply comes in. You juggle. And all of a sudden you find yourself hopping between 20 threads, trying to keep all those contexts in your brain RAM. Until you can't. Your brain gets exhausted, your focus smashes, and you don't know anymore what you were doing, where you started, and where you were supposed to finish. A lot of people are suggesting taking breaks, thinking before typing, limiting scope. I have my own experiment. I decided this way of working has two major problems: sequencing and context. So I organised my work a bit like a priority queue. Here is how it actually works. The queue lives in git. Every ticket is a markdown file in the repo, right next to the code it talks about, and the state of the board is a committed snapshot. Nothing important lives in a chat window and nothing lives in my head. If a session dies, the queue is still there. An agent works that board in cycles. It researches new tickets, builds the ones a human has tagged as safe to build, runs the tests and a browser check, and verifies what is already deployed. For anything touching sensitive code it builds on a branch and asks first. It never deploys to production — that part is mine. What it cannot do is decide. So everything that needs me lands in one place I call my owner inbox. A script reads the whole board and hands me a prioritised list of exactly the items waiting on my judgement — review this change, answer this question, rule on this tradeoff. The reading surface is a Claude artifact. One page, rebuilt from git on every cycle, mirroring the whole board plus a review page per ticket. items.full_text_snippet: < img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400"> GitHub不堪重负！OpenAI收购替代品，A社原地自研，马斯克也要搞 听雨 2026-11-07 17:38:56 来源： 量子位 听雨 发自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公众号QbitAI GitHub，你怎么又出故障了…… 11月3日，官方状态页一天就记下了两起故障，其中一起影响Git操作。 到了4日，合并请求等服务又出现异常，部分请求失败或延迟。 代码改好了，想让同事看看能不能并进主项目，偏偏卡在了这一步。 还有网友因此打趣： 正好去喝杯咖啡。 就在GitHub忙着抢修的时候，Axios发出一条独家消息： OpenAI拟收购做代码托管工具的Pierre ，交易仍待交割。 这两条消息撞在一起，时间有点赶巧啊。 而且不得不说，做AI编程工具的公司，还真有好几家开始自己管代码了。 马斯克旗下的Cursor，已经允许开发者把整个项目直接存在Cursor里。 Anthropic更进一步，把自家工程师天天用的主代码库搬进了自研系统。 几家公司为什么都开始折腾这件事？ 因为AI写代码的速度越来越快，基础设施已经逐渐跟不上了…… OpenAI自己造了一个，还准备再买一家 OpenAI自己就尝过代码系统跟不上的滋味。 今年3月，The Information就报道过，OpenAI工程师多次遇到GitHub服务中断，公司正在开发内部替代工具。 到了11月2日——就在前几天，它公开了自己的Git后端 Pando ，负责承接内部代码的存取等操作。 据工程团队介绍，以前，一个工程师手里推进一份改动。有了Codex，一个人可以同时准备好几份。 而每推送一次代码，又会触发多个自动化任务，去取代码、运行检查。 写代码的人没有突然多出好几倍，系统要处理的工作却增加了。 原来的系统渐渐吃力，拉取、推送变慢，合并也会失败。 Pando从4月起就开始承接真实的开发流量。按OpenAI的统计，换上之后，一次推送的中位耗时降了近八成。 自家工程师的问题解决了，面向Codex用户，OpenAI还准备通过收购 Pierre ，把代码存储等能力带进产品里。 说起来，Pierre的东西，你可能已经用过了～ 假设你让Codex修一个bug，它一口气改了五个文件。 你点开文件列表，找到其中一个，再逐行对照它删了什么、加了什么。 前一个动作，用的是Pierre做的Trees；后一个，用的是Pierre做的Diffs。这两套工具早就接进了Codex。 Pierre还有一门生意叫 Code Storage ，它的客户里，就有AI应用开发平台Lovable。 用户在Lovable里输入几句话，就能做出一个网站。在后台，每个项目都要用一个或多个Git仓库来保存代码和修改历史。 据Pierre今年8月披露的数据，当时Lovable 每周新建超过800万个仓库 ，峰值达到每秒250个。 OpenAI打算等收购完成，再把Code Storage的能力带进Codex。 以后，开发者让AI写代码、查看它改了哪里，再把这一版存下来，都有望在Codex里完成。 目前，这笔交易还要满足监管批准等交割条件。 Cursor开放代码托管那天，GitHub也挂了 大家可能还记得，8月14日，马斯克的SpaceX完成对Cursor的收购。 三天后，Cursor的代码托管服务Origin开放早期测试。 结果偏偏就在8月17日，GitHub也发生了一场持续 7小时47分钟 的故障。 Cursor员工Matt Palmer当时还开了个玩笑，大意是，他们本来想更早发的，可GitHub，它、它又挂了！！ Origin给了开发者两种选择：做新项目，可以直接在Origin建仓库，代码推到Cursor，请同事审、接收修改意见、合并分支，这些操作都能绕开GitHub。 老项目如果已经放在GitHub，也可以只同步一份到Cursor。 你在Cursor里留下的评论，队友回到GitHub也能看到，代码仍以GitHub上的版本为准。 那问题就来了： 写代码、审代码、合并，都能在Cursor里办完了，那我还专门打开GitHub干啥？ 哪怕是老项目，仓库还放在GitHub，但审代码的人也已经可以不去那儿了。 Claude写得太快，Anthropic自己造了一套 OpenAI和Cursor把更多开发操作接进了自己的产品，而到了Anthropic内部，工作量已经大到需要重做代码管理系统。 主要还是因为，Claude写代码写得太快了…… items.full_text_snippet: Since November 5, 2026, Microsoft's consumer mail service has been turning away some of the email from domains that don't publish a DMARC record. If your company emails customers, vendors or applicants with outlook.com, hotmail.com, live.com or msn.com addresses, some of that mail may be bouncing right now. Nobody announced it. The fix is one DNS record. Key takeaways Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live and MSN now refuse part of the mail from domains that have no DMARC record. It hits ordinary, low-volume senders, not only the bulk senders Microsoft's published rules cover. Only some messages bounce, so "my mail is getting through" doesn't mean your domain is safe. The fix is a single TXT record, v=DMARC1; p=none , which changes nothing about how other receivers treat your mail. What the bounce looks like The sender gets a bounce like this one, followed by a bracketed server name and ID that differ per message: 550 5.7.1 Message rejected: Message lacks SPF/DKIM/DMARC Auth Records (AS9031519) On the first day, the same rejection came back without the (AS9031519) code: 550 5.7.1 Message rejected: Message lacks SPF/DKIM/DMARC Auth Records The wording suggests something is badly broken. Usually it isn't. The domains we have seen bounced mostly had working SPF, and many had DKIM too. What they were missing was the DMARC record that ties the two to the From address. What changed Microsoft does have published sender rules. Since May 2025, domains that send more than 5,000 messages a day to Outlook.com have had to pass SPF, DKIM and DMARC, or get 550 5.7.515 Access denied . That rule is aimed at marketers and bulk senders, and most small businesses rightly assumed it didn't apply to them. This new rejection is different in the ways that matter: It reaches small senders. A one-line reply from a small office can bounce. It wasn't announced. As of November 6, Microsoft has published nothing about it: no postmaster notice, no blog post, no service-health entry. items.full_text_snippet: Sam Altman is not having a good couple of weeks; ever since he said OpenAI’s ram needs are more important than consumer electronics, the internet has been unforgiving. But one man has taken things one step further to mock Altman’s ridiculous super villain sounding statements. Open-source developer Iain Kay has created an open-source BASH script called “ Ram Altman ” for Linux systems designed to monitor how much idle RAM you have sitting on your rigs, laptops, etc. The percentage of unused RAM is than emailed to Sam Altman… well not really. The correspondence depends on how you set it up. By default, the email server isn’t set up out of the box. The creator intentionally designed it this way to prevent the repository from being used as an automated mail-spoofing or denial-of-service tool against OpenAI’s servers. If a system has more than 10% of its total RAM available, “Ram-Altman” selects from a rotating bank of sarcastic email templates: “Hi Sam,” reads one of the sample messages. “Please don’t be alarmed, but there is 8.6 GiB of RAM on my desk that isn’t in a data centre. That’s 56.2% of what’s installed here, and as far as I can tell it has no plans today. Hoarding responsibly, A concerned RAM owner.” For sysadmins and Linux users hesitant to spam external mail servers, the repository includes a –dry-run flag and a local test suite. This allows users to test simulated memory workloads and preview the exact message generated without dispatching actual correspondence. Unless the user has the technical know-how on how to set it up that way. The project’s FAQ page is also pretty funny: Does this help with the DRAM shortage? “No.” Does it work on macOS? “No, it reads /proc/meminfo. On the other hand, your RAM is probably soldered down, which makes you the hardest target in the global allocation programme.” Why is the threshold 10%? “Below that, your machine has suffered enough.” Does running this use RAM? “Briefly.
